The failing test `testStop3` in `PosixParserTest` is checking if the `PosixParser` stops processing tokens correctly after encountering a non-unrecognized long option while `stopAtNonOption` is enabled. In the failing scenario, after encountering the non-unrecognized long option "--zop==1", the subsequent tokens are being interpreted incorrectly.

By looking at the `PosixParser` implementation, specifically the `parse` method in the `CommandLineParser` interface, we see that it is responsible for parsing the arguments according to the specified options.

The issue in the failing test seems to be related to how the options are being parsed by the `PosixParser`. It appears that the parsing logic does not handle the non-unrecognized long option "--zop==1" and the subsequent tokens correctly.

To fix this issue, the parsing logic in the `PosixParser` implementation needs to be adjusted to correctly handle non-unrecognized long options and stop processing tokens after encountering them.

Next, I will suggest the method to be fixed.
The corresponding issue can be addressed by fixing the parsing logic in the `org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLineParser.parse` method.

Please consider fixing:
```
org.apache.commons.cli.CommandLineParser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[])
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
